subject: Post-demo: Observability interop validation checklist & next tests
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir@edgecloud.ai>, Ava Green <ava@edgecloud.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Observability interop validation checklist & next tests

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion. Quick recap and a concrete set of validation tests so we can close the observational gaps you called out during the demo. Goal is to make the POC measurable and map directly to your internal SLAs.

Summary of what we heard from EdgeCloud:
- Need per-route latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and token-level cost breakdowns for billing attribution.
- Want tracing correlation across platform services (request-id propagation: EdgeCloud API -> Redwood runtime -> your backend).
- Prefer Datadog as primary telemetry sink; also need exportable CSVs for finance.
- Concerned about graceful fallback when dedicated capacity/region is saturated.

Proposed validation checklist (suggested order):
1) End-to-end trace correlation: send a synthetic workload where EdgeCloud injects X-Trace-Id; verify trace appears in Datadog with span for Redwood token generation and KV cache hits. Acceptance: trace contains request, model, and runtime spans with duration metadata.
2) Per-route dashboarding: enable per-route dashboards for a small set (chatgen, rerank). Acceptance: dashboards show p50/p95/p99 and tokens-per-request in Datadog and a CSV export for 24h.
3) Tail latency tests: 1000 concurrent short requests and 200 long-context requests during burst window. Acceptance: 99th percentile < 250ms for short requests in us-west, and clear fallback behavior documented if thresholds breached.
4) Cost delta vs hyperscaler baseline: run identical prompt set through your current hyperscaler endpoint and through Redwood-hosted config (same model family). Acceptance: token cost delta and quality anchors in the shared spreadsheet.
5) Failure & fallback verification: simulate model OOM and regional outage; acceptance: automatic fallback to compatible variant and correct error telemetry.

Deliverables we will provide by Monday:
- POC runbook (attached as "edgecloud-poc-plan.pdf") with step-by-step test commands and expected Datadog queries.
- A redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx prefilled with fields for latency, cost, and instrumentation gaps.

Ask from your side:
- Confirm which Datadog team + API key we should use for test ingest (or a temp test API key).
- Signal any additional traces/labels you require (e.g., customer_id tag).
- Preferred 2-hour window for running the burst tests next week (timezone: PDT).

I'll schedule an internal alignment meeting (Marissa + Ben + infra) and then a coordinated run with your engineering team.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai

Thanks Rafael — this is super helpful. A few clarifications from our side before we lock windows:

- Datadog: we'll spin up a test API key and give you write-only access to a staging org. I'll DM the key to Samir and Rafael. Does Redwood have a recommended tags schema? We want to preserve our edge_region and customer_tier labels.
- For the cost delta: what exactly do you need on the prompt set? We can provide a 500-prompt anonymized corpus. Any size/format constraints?
- Fallback behavior: if Redwood falls back to a smaller quantized variant, will you preserve deterministic sampling (same seed) so we can do a quality diff?

Also, any chance Marissa can join our platform sync on Mon 7/13 10:00-10:30am PDT to walk through Datadog dashboards?

Regards,
Ava Green

Thanks, Ava — answers inline below.

- Tags schema: we recommend these baseline tags: request_id, customer_id, route, model_variant, region, edge_region, customer_tier. We'll send a sample tagging JSON in the Drive doc. It's fine to keep your edge_region and customer_tier — we'll consume them.
- Prompt set: 500 anonymized prompts in a plain .csv (columns: prompt_id, prompt_text). If you can also include a 50-prompt subset for manual QA, that helps for quality anchors.
- Deterministic fallback: yes — when falling back to a quantized variant we can preserve deterministic seeds for sampled decoding and log the seed in telemetry so you can replay. Note: slight differences possible if kernels/quantization change sampling behavior, we'll include a note in the runbook.

On Mon 7/13 10:00am PDT Marissa will join to walk the dashboards — that's on our calendar.

I'll put the final POC runbook in Drive and share the HubSpot record with the tasks.

Rafael

Quick technical notes from our side before the run:

1) Datadog ingestion: use OTLP/HTTP with our recommended batch size. We'll provide a config snippet for ingestion that maps runtime spans to Datadog APM service names.
2) Trace sampling: for the burst test we suggest 100% local sampling for 30 minutes, then drop to 5% to preserve costs. We'll bake sampling into the runbook.
3) KV cache visibility: we'll emit a metric for cache_hit_ratio per-model per-route — please surface that in your dashboard so you can see the effectiveness of warm caches.
4) CSV exports: we'll add a lightweight export endpoint that dumps per-route token/cost aggregates to CSV hourly during the POC run.

If EdgeCloud can provide a small list of 3 representative routes and the Datadog test org, we'll stand up the run on Tue/Wed next week depending on your window.

—Marissa
